mil3.4.2:1.7: “But venerable sir, does one cognize all of salt with the tongue?”
mil3.4.2:1.8: “Yes, Great King, one cognizes all of salt with the tongue.”
mil3.4.2:2.1: “If, venerable sir, one cognizes all of salt with the tongue, why do they haul it with carts and oxen? Should not salt alone be brought?”
mil3.4.2:2.2: “It is not possible, Great King, to bring salt alone, since these phenomena have come together as one, differing in their range: salt and heaviness.
mil3.4.2:2.3: But is it possible, Great King, to weigh salt on a scale?”
mil3.4.2:2.5: “It is not possible, Great King, to weigh salt on a scale; it is heaviness that is weighed on a scale.”
